learningPaths.title: Echocardiography simulator: learn the standard echo views
learningPaths.description: Explore 15 echo views with probe-position guides and EchoSuite’s interactive 3D Probe Lab.
learningPaths.intro: Build familiarity with the standard views by pairing each acquisition guide with its matching probe and mannequin view in Probe Lab. Use Practice to explore the probe controls and acquisition coaching.

steps.title: Start with the parasternal views
steps.body: Open parasternal long axis, then explore the short-axis levels. Each guide has the probe position, acquisition wording and image-optimization notes used in the lab.

steps.title: Explore the apical views
steps.body: Move between the four-, five-, two- and three-chamber guides and their corresponding views in Probe Lab.

steps.title: Find the subcostal and right-heart views
steps.body: Explore the subcostal four-chamber and IVC views, then compare the RV inflow and outflow views. Read each acquisition guide before opening its practice target.

steps.title: Continue to the aorta
steps.body: Finish the view collection with the abdominal aorta and suprasternal aortic arch guides, then return to any view for more practice.

learningPaths.title: Aortic stenosis: from echo views to the continuity equation
learningPaths.description: Connect LVOT and aortic echo views with the aortic valve area calculator, acquisition teaching and primary references.
learningPaths.intro: Follow the existing guides from probe views to the measurements used by EchoSuite’s aortic stenosis tool. Open the interactive calculator for its acquisition figures, method choices and reference context.

steps.title: Explore the relevant echo views
steps.body: Review parasternal long axis and the apical five- and three-chamber views in the acquisition guides and Probe Lab.

steps.title: Review LVOT flow measurements
steps.body: Open the LVOT stroke-volume and cardiac-output guide to review the measurements, units, formula and sources. The calculator’s How it works section contains its acquisition teaching.

steps.title: Explore aortic valve area
steps.body: Continue to the aortic stenosis continuity tool. Try its worked example, inspect the formula and browse the references alongside the method’s qualifications.

learningPaths.title: Left ventricular volumes and ejection fraction: a learning path
learningPaths.description: Explore apical views, LV volume indexing and the ejection fraction calculator with acquisition guidance and sources.
learningPaths.intro: Connect the apical view guides with EchoSuite’s LV volume and ejection fraction tools. Keep the selected measurement method and its references together as you explore.

steps.title: Explore the apical four- and two-chamber views
steps.body: Read the acquisition and image-optimization notes, then open the matching views in Probe Lab.

steps.title: Review volume measurements and indexing
steps.body: Explore the LV volumes tool’s method choices and measurement guidance. The body surface area tool provides a separate place to review height, weight and units.

steps.title: Work through ejection fraction
steps.body: Open the LVEF calculator and try the worked example. Compare the entered volumes with the formula, then explore the acquisition teaching and the references for the chosen method.

learningPaths.title: Right-heart echocardiography: views, measurements and calculators
learningPaths.description: Explore right-heart echo views and the RV size, RV function, right atrial pressure and RVSP calculators.
learningPaths.intro: Use the existing view and measurement guides to navigate EchoSuite’s right-heart tools. Each calculator retains its own acquisition requirements, method limits and reference context.

steps.title: Explore the right-heart views
steps.body: Start with apical four chamber, RV inflow and RV outflow. Read each view’s acquisition notes and open the matching Probe Lab view.

steps.title: Browse chamber size and RV function
steps.body: Explore the right atrial size, RV size and RV function tools. Their acquisition teaching and reference sections can be browsed alongside the measurement inputs.

steps.title: Continue to pressure estimates
steps.body: Read the IVC view guide, then explore the right atrial pressure and RVSP/PASP tools. Review the required signals and qualifications in each calculator.

acquisition.move: Place the patient left lateral, set the probe beside the sternum, and aim through the LV long axis.
acquisition.optimization: Slide one interspace at a time and maximize LV length without showing papillary muscle.
acquisition.contact: 3rd-4th interspace, immediately left of the sternum

acquisition.move: Place the probe at the true apical impulse and aim medially toward the base of the heart.
acquisition.optimization: Avoid foreshortening: center a pointed apex and maximize both ventricles and atria.
acquisition.contact: At the apical impulse, low and lateral on the left chest

acquisition.move: With the patient supine, flatten the probe below the xiphoid and aim toward the left shoulder using the liver as the window.
acquisition.optimization: Use held inspiration if helpful and keep both septa perpendicular to the beam.
acquisition.contact: Immediately inferior to the xiphoid, aimed beneath the costal margin

acquisition.move: From subcostal four chamber, rotate counterclockwise to a sagittal plane and aim through the liver toward the RA.
acquisition.optimization: Show several centimeters of IVC entering the RA and include a full respiratory cycle.
acquisition.contact: Just right of midline, immediately inferior to the xiphoid

acquisition.move: Keep the probe sagittal, slide slightly left of midline, and angle posteriorly until the aorta lies over the vertebral body.
acquisition.optimization: Confirm a pulsatile thick-walled vessel anterior to the spine and follow it longitudinally.
acquisition.contact: Just left of midline, immediately inferior to the xiphoid

acquisition.move: Extend the neck, place the probe in the notch, and aim toward the plane between the right nipple and left scapular tip.
acquisition.optimization: Trace the ascending, transverse, and descending arch and identify the branch vessels when possible.
acquisition.contact: In the suprasternal notch with the neck gently extended

views.name: Parasternal short axis, aortic valve level

acquisition.move: Rotate about 90° clockwise from PLAX, then tilt superiorly toward the base until the aortic valve is centered.
acquisition.optimization: Avoid oblique cuts; center the aortic valve with the surrounding right-heart structures.
acquisition.contact: 3rd-4th interspace, immediately left of the sternum

views.name: Parasternal short axis, mitral valve level

acquisition.move: From PSAX aortic level, tilt inferiorly until the mitral leaflets form the fish-mouth appearance.
acquisition.optimization: Show the entire mitral orifice with symmetric anterior and posterior leaflet motion.
acquisition.contact: 3rd-4th interspace, immediately left of the sternum

views.name: Parasternal short axis, papillary muscle level

acquisition.move: Continue tilting inferiorly toward the apex until both papillary muscles are seen within a circular LV.
acquisition.optimization: Keep the LV circular and both papillary muscles visible; an oval LV usually means an oblique cut.
acquisition.contact: 3rd-4th interspace, immediately left of the sternum

acquisition.move: Continue the inferior sweep toward the apex until the papillary muscles disappear and the LV cavity becomes small.
acquisition.optimization: Sweep until the LV cavity nearly disappears so apical disease is not missed.
acquisition.contact: Start left parasternal; slide 1-2 spaces inferior and lateral if needed

acquisition.move: From PLAX, tilt inferiorly toward the patient’s right hip; add slight counterclockwise rotation to center the tricuspid valve.
acquisition.optimization: Center the tricuspid valve and include substantial RV and RA; avoid drifting back into PLAX.
acquisition.contact: 3rd-4th interspace, immediately left of the sternum

acquisition.move: From PLAX, tilt anteriorly and rotate slightly clockwise until the RVOT, pulmonary valve, and main PA appear.
acquisition.optimization: Show two pulmonary-valve leaflets and as much of the main PA as possible.
acquisition.contact: 3rd-4th interspace, immediately left of the sternum

acquisition.move: Keep the A4C contact point and tilt the beam anteriorly until the LVOT and aortic valve enter the center.
acquisition.optimization: Use only enough anterior tilt to open the LVOT; excessive tilt loses chamber length.
acquisition.contact: At the apical impulse, low and lateral on the left chest

acquisition.move: From A4C, rotate roughly 60° counterclockwise without sliding off the apex.
acquisition.optimization: Exclude the right heart and maximize LV length; show the anterior and inferior walls.
acquisition.contact: At the apical impulse, low and lateral on the left chest

acquisition.move: From A2C, rotate roughly another 60° counterclockwise to bring in the LVOT, aortic valve, and aorta.
acquisition.optimization: Align the LV, LVOT, aortic valve, and ascending aorta in one continuous long axis.
acquisition.contact: At the apical impulse, low and lateral on the left chest

evidence.label: Mosteller
evidence.supports: BSA = √(H × W / 3600). H in cm, W in kg, BSA in m². The app defaults to this equation; this is not a claim that every echo reference uses it.

evidence.label: Du Bois & Du Bois
evidence.supports: BSA = 0.007184 × H^0.725 × W^0.425; H in cm and W in kg.

evidence.label: Haycock, Schwartz & Wisotsky
evidence.supports: BSA = 0.024265 × H^0.3964 × W^0.5378; H in cm and W in kg. The primary study included infants, children and adults.

evidence.label: Gehan & George
evidence.supports: BSA = 0.0235 × H^0.42246 × W^0.51456; H in cm and W in kg.

evidence.label: Body size and indexed valve area
